PC:
Ask appropriate questions (directed history-taking):
History of chest pain.
Onset, provoking/alleviating factors, quality, radiation, severity, time course.
Cardiac risk factors (hypertension, diabetes, dyslipidemia, smoking, illicit drug use, Family history).
Bleeding risk factors (GIB, anemia).
Previous cardiac workup.
Recent ASA/nitro/illicit/Sildenafil use.
Perform a physical examination (ask specific questions re: findings).

Order appropriate labs:
ECG and Chest X-ray (CXR) – ask student to interpret.
CBC, basic metabolic panel, cardiac enzymes, coagulation studies.

Start appropriate treatment:
Recognize **not** to give nitroglycerin (NTG) due to inferior MI
Aspirin
Morphine
+/- Heparin or plavix
Re-order ECG – ask student to interpret.

Check if stable/unstable:
Stable: Observe, continue MI work-up-our patient is NOT stable.
Unstable: Start ACLS:

Medical Therapy will NOT improve bradycardia:
atropine (0.5mg)
dopamine (2-10mcg/kg/min infusion)
epinephrine (2-10mcg/min)

Transcutaneous Pacing is required to improve heart rate and symptoms
Increase voltage until “capture”
Call cardiology for tranvenous pacemaker placement (for more definitive care)
SBP: Consult cardiology to discuss need for cardiac catheterization.
